meta.description: Analyzes base-editing screens for variant function: library design (Hanna 2021 ClinVar-scale CBE screen, Cuella-Martin 2021 DDR saturation), CBE vs ABE chemistry choice, editing-window math (positions 4-8 from PAM-distal end), bystander-edit quantification, sgRNA-efficiency filtering before hit calling, indel byproduct interpretation, ClinVar/COSMIC annotation, and the Broad be-validation-pipeline.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated statistics, DOIs, or trial results. Editing-window values, chemistry tables, and Hanna/Cuella-Martin methodology summaries are unchanged from the pre-fix audit's PASS and still match the cited primary literature.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research-scope screen/variant-function analysis only; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about a person or patient.

methodological_ground.detail: Editing-window math, chemistry selection logic, and the substitution-vs-indel diagnostic are methodologically sound; independently re-confirmed in both directions this pass (real Cas9-nuclease sample correctly Cas9-like, real clean-BE sample correctly non-Cas9-like).

code_usability.detail: All 4 of the previously-crashing/silently-wrong bundled functions now run correctly against real CRISPResso2 2.3.4 and real MAGeCK 0.5.9.5 output, reproducing planted ground truth exactly: filter_by_editing_efficiency() (50.0%/30.0% target/bystander editing), deconvolute_bystander() (40/30/20/10 allele partition), aggregate_variant_scores() (merges on real lowercase 'sgrna', per-variant LFC mean matches a by-hand recomputation), and find_be_spacers() (reverse-strand coordinate conversion independently verified correct on a hand-constructed case built to trigger the OPPOSITE failure direction from the fixer's own test, plus on a fresh randomly-generated CDS with genuine reverse-strand on-target hits). One NEW, previously-unreported defect was found and is reported below as P1, not a veto trigger: find_be_spacers() raises a bare, unrelated KeyError('n_bystanders') instead of a clear message when it finds zero candidate spacers (e.g. a short CDS, or a lowercase-masked input against the case-sensitive PAM regex) -- a real robustness gap on a boundary condition, not a break in the core, now-verified-correct happy path.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness unchanged (strong). Correctness now confirmed positive: all 4 bundled functions run correctly on real CRISPResso2/MAGeCK output and reproduce planted ground truth exactly, independently re-verified this pass (not just the fixer's own claims). Docked 1 point for the newly-found zero-candidate crash in find_be_spacers().

reliability.note: 3 of 4 functions now validate their input schema and raise specific, actionable ValueErrors (verified against 5 adversarial malformed inputs, all 5 fired correctly with clear messages). find_be_spacers() still has no such validation: an invalid editor name raises a bare KeyError, and a zero-candidate result crashes with an unrelated-looking KeyError('n_bystanders') from an empty-DataFrame .sort_values() call -- both confirmed by execution, not inspection.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md/usage-guide.md duplication (the pre-fix P2) is fixed: both the Base Editor Chemistry Selection table and the editing-efficiency threshold convention are now single-sourced in SKILL.md with usage-guide.md cross-referencing it, confirmed by reading both files.

agent_usability.note: Strong learnability and decision trees, unchanged. Error Prevention and Feedback Design substantially improved: 3 of 4 functions now fail loudly with specific column/value names instead of bare KeyErrors. Docked 2 points: the inconsistency (find_be_spacers not covered) means an agent following the Skill still hits an unhelped crash on a plausible edge case.

human_usability.note: Forgiveness meaningfully improved: a researcher hitting the 3 fixed functions' errors now gets an actionable message naming the real problem. BE-Hive section gained a full runnable example plus an explicit warning to cross-check the substrate/spacer offset before trusting output -- verified this actually prevents the exact 1nt-frameshift mistake the pre-fix audit made by hand.

security.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: no secrets or injection vectors; inputs are sequence strings, file paths, and column names. Still no input-range validation for target_aa/target_base types beyond what the new schema checks cover.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples split, unchanged. Testability improved: 3 of 4 functions are now demonstrably run-tested against real tool output per the fix log and this audit's own independent reruns. find_be_spacers() has no bundled test/assertion of its own despite being the most subtly-defective function pre-fix; this audit's hand-constructed regression (input2) fills that gap externally but nothing in the Skill itself would catch a regression.

agent_specific.note: Precise triggering and excellent Related-Skills composability, unchanged. Escape Hatches improved: 3 of 4 functions now give an agent a specific, parseable error to act on. Docked 3 points for the newly-found gap: no escape hatch at all when find_be_spacers() finds zero candidates -- an agent gets a confusing internal pandas KeyError with no path to recovery.

inputs.label: Hand-constructed reverse-strand regression for the P0 coordinate-conversion fix (find_be_spacers)
inputs.note: The single most important regression in this audit. Built, before running any code, a 100nt CDS engineered so the true on-target edited base sits at forward-CDS index 88 (inside codon [87,90)) but reverse-complement index 11 -- the OPPOSITE failure direction from the fixer's own test case (which found a false on-target; this construction targets a false negative / missed target instead, to check the fix is a general coordinate conversion and not tuned to one direction). Hand-derived prediction: unconverted math would call it a bystander (11 not in [87,90)); converted math correctly calls it target (88 is in [87,90)). Ran the fixed function: it returned exactly one engineered candidate with target_positions=[5], bystander_positions=[] -- matching the hand-derived correct answer, not the pre-fix bug's answer.

recommendations.title: find_be_spacers() crashes with a bare, unrelated KeyError when it finds zero candidate spacers
recommendations.problem: When no PAM-adjacent window contains the target base on either strand (a short CDS, an unlucky sequence for a narrow-window editor, or a lowercase-masked input against the case-sensitive [ACGT]GG PAM regex), `candidates` stays empty and `pd.DataFrame(candidates).sort_values('n_bystanders')` raises `KeyError: 'n_bystanders'` -- a confusing error unrelated to the actual problem (no candidates found), with no guidance for the agent.
recommendations.root_cause: pd.DataFrame([]) has no columns at all, so .sort_values() on a column name that would only exist if candidates were non-empty fails. This is the same class of defect (missing schema/edge-case guard) that the fix pass addressed in the other 3 functions, but find_be_spacers() was not covered.
recommendations.fix: Guard the return: `if not candidates: return pd.DataFrame(columns=['spacer','strand','spacer_start','target_positions','bystander_positions','n_bystanders'])` before the .sort_values() call, so callers get a well-formed empty result (or raise a clear ValueError like 'no candidate spacers found for target_aa=... with editor=...') instead of an internal pandas KeyError.

recommendations.title: find_be_spacers() has no editor-name validation, unlike the schema-checked functions
recommendations.problem: Calling find_be_spacers() with an invalid `editor` string raises a bare `KeyError: 'NOT_A_REAL_EDITOR'` from the window_by_editor dict lookup, rather than a clear message listing the valid editor names.
recommendations.root_cause: window_by_editor[editor] is indexed directly with no existence check, the same pattern the fix pass replaced with explicit ValueErrors in the other 3 functions.
recommendations.fix: Add `if editor not in window_by_editor: raise ValueError(f"editor={editor!r} not recognized; valid editors: {sorted(window_by_editor)}")` at the top of the function, consistent with the validation style already added elsewhere in this Skill.
